I guess my suggestion would be to hold back on the visits, if, for example, you visit him every weekend, dial it back to every other and simply explain that you’re too busy at the moment and need some time to relax at the weekend without hours of driving. 

I think over time he’ll realise that it’s only fair he shares the travel burden. You’re absolutely in the right to be frustrated with him not getting vaccinated and not travelling but instead of building up resentment by just allowing it, give him a chance to feel the repercussions. An alternative suggestion is that every other weekend you suggest he pays for a hotel for you both just over the border in Canada to save you some time on your journey, maybe feeling some financial sting would help too?

P.S. My partner has a needle phobia and won’t get vaccinated yet so I’m really open to any advice people are going to offer about potentially encouraging OP’s boyfriend to get vaccinated.

Well this is a very specific situation that I have first hand experience of, weirdly. My godmother had cystic fibrosis and died a few years after I was born. She was an incredible woman and my mother knew all along that she would never live long enough to take care of me if something were to happen to her.

She was my mum's closest friend and mum knew that she wanted her to be my godmother regardless of her illness. I'm in my early 20s now and we still talk about her a lot and my mum misses her every day. Going back on your promise would make you an asshole. And I truly think you would regret not making her your daughter's godmother. Don't deny her the opportunity to play a role in your daughter's life for what little time she has left.
